titleStmt.title: A Feminist Approach to Linked Open Data: Making the Women Film Pioneers Project FAIR
titleStmt.author: Pauline Junginger

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: A Feminist Approach to Linked Open Data: Making the Women Film Pioneers Project FAIR

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: How can research data in feminist film historiography be modelled as Linked Open Data when categorisation reduces the very plurality and gaps the field exists to record?
span.quote: How can the plurality of feminist film historiography be accounted for when modeling research data as LOD requires categorization and standardization, and thus a reduction of complexity?

span.label: Reports a reversal: from building a project thesaurus to reusing existing ones, and what that cost in categories.
span.quote: While the initial goal of the project was to develop a thesaurus tailored to the needs of WFPP’s staff and users, it became clear as the project progressed that a more promising approach would be to focus on reusing existing thesauri to make the data FAIR.

span.label: method
span.quote: Therefore, my project aims to create structured metadata for the WFPP, enrich it with authority data, and link it in a sustainable way to other datasets on women film pioneers.

span.label: linked open data for feminist film historiography
span.quote: By creating FAIR metadata using the WFPP filmographies as an example, the project explores how the FAIR principles can be applied in feminist film historiography.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Second, whereas the initial concept included a manual text analysis and annotation with CATMA to build the thesaurus in a bottom-up approach, the filmographic data is now extracted using Named Entity Recognition and then modeled as LOD.

span.label: Reusing existing thesauri rather than building one forces the project's categories down to those that carry across datasets, which is what makes the data linkable at all
span.quote: This conceptual shift from developing a project-specific thesaurus to opening up the collection by sustainably linking disparate datasets on women film pioneers had several implications for the project's methodological design.

span.label: Extraction moves from manual annotation to named entity recognition once the target is linked data rather than a bespoke vocabulary
span.quote: Second, whereas the initial concept included a manual text analysis and annotation with CATMA to build the thesaurus in a bottom-up approach, the filmographic data is now extracted using Named Entity Recognition and then modeled as LOD.

span.label: Existing authority files are treated as objects of evaluation rather than given infrastructure, because their fitness for feminist film history is not assumed
span.quote: Third, an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File (VIAF), Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), and Wikidata regarding their usability for feminist film historiography.

span.label: The paper reports only preliminary results; it is a poster describing a methodological approach rather than a completed, evaluated system.
span.quote: This poster outlines the methodological approach of the project and presents preliminary results.

span.label: The scope was narrowed mid-project from nine modelling categories to four, restricting coverage to filmographic data.
span.quote: First, the nine categories initially identified for modeling the thesaurus (person, film work, occupation, place, technique, institution, film genre, theme, and publication) were reduced to four categories relevant to the structured collection of filmographies: person, film work, institution, and place.

span.label: The authors state as an open problem that LOD modelling forces categorisation, standardisation and a reduction of complexity that may not accommodate the plurality of feminist film historiography.
span.quote: How can the plurality of feminist film historiography be accounted for when modeling research data as LOD requires categorization and standardization, and thus a reduction of complexity?

span.label: Modelling as LOD requires standardisation, which reduces exactly the complexity the field is trying to preserve
span.quote: How can the plurality of feminist film historiography be accounted for when modeling research data as LOD requires categorization and standardization, and thus a reduction of complexity?

span.label: Classification is taken to be never neutral, so the vocabularies being reused carry values that are not the project's own
span.quote: How can we incorporate feminist values into the design of categories if we assume that classification practices are never neutral but always entangled with political attitudes and values (Bowker / Star 1999; Drabinski 2013; D'Ignazio / Klein 2020)?

span.label: The gaps left by lost sources and undocumented feminized labour have no obvious representation in a data model
span.quote: In the context of feminist film historiography, we also have to ask how the numerous blind spots and knowledge gaps that exist due to lost sources and the limited documentation of "feminized labor" (Hill 2016: 5) can be represented in data-based approaches (Dang 2020).

span.label: The poster reports an approach and preliminary results rather than outcomes, so nothing here is yet evaluated
span.quote: This poster outlines the methodological approach of the project and presents preliminary results.

span.label: authority file
span.quote: an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File

span.label: Virtual International Authority File
span.quote: an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File

span.label: thesaurus - project-specific: built bottom-up for this resource's own staff and users, which was the original plan
span.quote: While the initial goal of the project was to develop a thesaurus tailored to the needs of WFPP’s staff and users, it became clear as the project progressed that a more promising approach would be to focus on reusing existing thesauri to make the data FAIR.

span.label: thesaurus - existing and reused: an external vocabulary adopted so the data links outward, which is what the project switched to
span.quote: Third, an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File (VIAF), Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), and Wikidata regarding their usability for feminist film historiography.

span.label: categories - the nine identified for modelling a thesaurus, covering the resource's whole conceptual range
span.quote: First, the nine categories initially identified for modeling the thesaurus (person, film work, occupation, place, technique, institution, film genre, theme, and publication) were reduced to four categories relevant to the structured collection of filmographies: person, film work, institution, and place.

span.label: categories - the four kept for filmographies, which is what survived the decision to link outward
span.quote: were reduced to four categories relevant to the structured collection of filmographies: person, film work, institution, and place

span.label: builds-on → digital humanities work on text as data, digital publishing, categorization practices and metadata (Blaney et al. 2021; Flanders / Jannidis 2018)
span.quote: In addition to feminist film historiography, the digital humanities are a central point of reference for this project, particularly approaches that address accessibility of text as data, digital publishing, categorization practices, and metadata (Blaney et al. 2021; Flanders / Jannidis 2018).

span.label: builds-on → critical classification scholarship (Bowker / Star 1999; Drabinski 2013; D'Ignazio / Klein 2020)
span.quote: How can we incorporate feminist values into the design of categories if we assume that classification practices are never neutral but always entangled with political attitudes and values (Bowker / Star 1999; Drabinski 2013; D'Ignazio / Klein 2020)?

span.label: extends → existing work modelling film heritage data as Linked Open Data, including Wikidata case studies
span.quote: In the field of film heritage institutions, the modeling of film data as Linked Open Data has been discussed for several years (Heftberger 2019), including case studies with Wikidata (Heftberger / Duchesne 2020).

span.label: supports → the position that classification practices are never neutral (Bowker & Star, Drabinski, D'Ignazio & Klein)
span.quote: How can we incorporate feminist values into the design of categories if we assume that classification practices are never neutral but always entangled with political attitudes and values (Bowker / Star 1999; Drabinski 2013; D'Ignazio / Klein 2020)?

span.label: Linked Open Data —operationalised-as→ FAIR data principles
span.quote: In order to make metadata interoperable in the sense of the FAIR data principles, it can be made available as Linked Open Data (Schmidt et al. 2022).

span.label: Wikidata —is-a→ authority data
span.quote: Third, an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File (VIAF), Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), and Wikidata regarding their usability for feminist film historiography.

span.label: Virtual International Authority File —is-a→ authority data
span.quote: such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File (VIAF), Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), and Wikidata

span.label: Named Entity Recognition —contrasted-with→ CATMA
span.quote: Second, whereas the initial concept included a manual text analysis and annotation with CATMA to build the thesaurus in a bottom-up approach, the filmographic data is now extracted using Named Entity Recognition and then modeled as LOD.

span.label: Named Entity Recognition —operationalised-as→ filmographies
span.quote: the filmographic data is now extracted using Named Entity Recognition and then modeled as LOD

span.label: categorization —causes→ feminist film historiography
span.quote: How can the plurality of feminist film historiography be accounted for when modeling research data as LOD requires categorization and standardization, and thus a reduction of complexity?

span.label: feminized labor —causes→ blind spots
span.quote: In the context of feminist film historiography, we also have to ask how the numerous blind spots and knowledge gaps that exist due to lost sources and the limited documentation of "feminized labor" (Hill 2016: 5) can be represented in data-based approaches (Dang 2020).

span.label: structured metadata —part-of→ Women Film Pioneers Project
span.quote: However, although structured metadata is central to making research data and digital publications visible, accessible, and reusable (Baca 2016; Flanders / Jannidis 2018), WFPP's application of metadata has been very limited.

span.label: categorization —part-of→ Semantic Web
span.quote: From a feminist perspective, when working with Linked Open Data, it is important to ask what assumptions, biases, and power relations are inscribed in Semantic Web technologies as well as in authority files and vocabularies.

span.label: thesaurus —contrasted-with→ authority data
span.quote: Therefore, my project aims to create structured metadata for the WFPP, enrich it with authority data, and link it in a sustainable way to other datasets on women film pioneers.

span.label: Virtual International Authority File —is-a→ authority file
span.quote: an important step in the methodology is to analyze and evaluate existing thesauri and authority files such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT), Friend of a Friend (FOAF), Virtual International Authority File

span.label: The project reversed its approach mid-way: reusing existing thesauri beat building its own.
span.quote: it became clear as the project progressed that a more promising approach would be to focus on reusing existing thesauri to make the data FAIR

span.label: That reversal cost coverage: nine modelling categories were cut to four.
span.quote: the nine categories initially identified for modeling the thesaurus (person, film work, occupation, place, technique, institution, film genre, theme, and publication) were reduced to four categories

span.label: Despite metadata being central to visibility and reuse, the resource's own metadata had been very limited.
span.quote: WFPP's application of metadata has been very limited

span.label: Women Film Pioneers Project
span.quote: The Women Film Pioneers Project (WFPP) is an established online resource for research on women in early cinema.

span.label: 9 → 4 — modelling categories before and after the shift to reusing existing thesauri
span.quote: were reduced to four categories relevant to the structured collection of filmographies

span.label: nine categories reduced to four — the concrete cost of switching from a bespoke thesaurus to reusable vocabularies
span.quote: First, the nine categories initially identified for modeling the thesaurus (person, film work, occupation, place, technique, institution, film genre, theme, and publication) were reduced to four categories relevant to the structured collection of filmographies: person, film work, institution, and place.
